record.paper_title: Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball: Recent Advances and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Topology of free boundary minimal submanifolds
record.original_question: Let Σ be a k-dimensional manifold, possibly immersed or embedded, inside the Euclidean unit ball B^n, with boundary on ∂B^n, such that Σ is minimal and meets ∂B^n orthogonally along its boundary; in other words, Σ is a free boundary minimal submanifold in B^n. What topological restrictions, if any, must Σ satisfy in order for such a free boundary minimal submanifold to exist? In particular, does the answer depend on whether one asks for immersed examples or embedded examples?

evidence.quote: Open Question 1. Are there any topological obstructions for a k-dimension submanifold Σ to be a free boundary minimal submanifold in B^n? Does it depend on whether Σ is immersed or embedded?

An immersed (resp. embedded) submanifold ϕ : Σ^k → B^n with ϕ(∂Σ) ⊂ ∂B^n is said to be an immersed (resp. embedded) free boundary minimal submanifold if both of the following holds: (i) Σ is a minimal submanifold (ii) Σ meets ∂B^n orthogonally along ∂Σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^n = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : |x| \le 1\}$ denote the closed Euclidean unit ball, with boundary $\partial B^n = S^{n-1}$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth $k$-dimensional manifold with boundary $\partial\Sigma$, and let $\phi : \Sigma \to B^n$ be a smooth immersion (respectively, embedding) such that $\phi(\partial\Sigma) \subset \partial B^n$ and $\phi(\mathrm{int}\,\Sigma) \subset \mathrm{int}\,B^n$. Call $\phi$ an immersed (resp. embedded) free boundary minimal submanifold if:
(i) $\phi(\Sigma)$ is a minimal submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^n$ (its mean curvature vector vanishes identically); and
(ii) $\phi(\Sigma)$ meets $\partial B^n$ orthogonally along $\phi(\partial\Sigma)$, i.e., at each boundary point the position vector (the outward unit normal to $\partial B^n$) lies in the tangent space of $\phi(\Sigma)$.

Determine all topological restrictions (if any) that the underlying manifold $\Sigma$ must satisfy in order for such an immersion (resp. embedding) into $B^n$ to exist. In particular, decide whether the set of admissible topological types of $\Sigma$ depends on whether one requires $\phi$ to be merely immersed or to be embedded.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of which topological types of $k$-manifolds admit free boundary minimal immersions/embeddings into $B^n$ remains open. Recent work (e.g., min-max constructions yielding free boundary minimal surfaces with prescribed genus and number of boundary components, and existence of new families in $B^3$) has produced many new examples but no general topological obstruction theorem, and the immersed-versus-embedded distinction has not been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Topological control for min-max free boundary minimal surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs embedded free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3 with controlled topology via min-max methods, indicating active progress but no general obstruction.
status_evidence.claim: New examples are still being constructed; the general topological classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: A Family of Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces in the Unit Ball
status_evidence.snippet: Provides new families of embedded free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3 with various genera and numbers of boundary components.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions continue to expand the list of realizable topologies; a complete answer is not known.

status_evidence.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball: recent advances and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing this as Open Question 1 on topological obstructions for free boundary minimal submanifolds in B^n.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as open in the survey literature.
